context_documents.title: Energy Calculator for Horizontal Piping (instructions, assumptions, form defaults and option lists)
quotes: Thermal conductivity based on ASTM Specification Values
Base structure is a horizontal steel pipe
Enter average wind speed for the period of operation (if unknown, use 1 mph for indoor, 8 mph for outdoor)
Installed costs of insulation are from industry sources and represent single layer installations

method.summary: One-dimensional steady state, horizontal steel pipe, inch-pound units. Per foot: q = π·D_s·(T_op − T_amb)/R_total, with R_total = R_wall + R_ins + 1/h_s referenced to the outer surface area. The outer surface temperature is iterated (T_s += error/2 until |error| < 1e-5°F) because h_s and the insulation mean k depend on it.

equations.steel_wall: R_wall = (D_s/2)·ln(OD/ID)/k_steel, k_steel = 458.46 − 0.1926·T − 1e-5·T² + 2e-8·T³ (Btu·in/h·ft²·°F, T = operating °F); Sch 40 OD/ID
equations.insulation: R_ins = (D_s/2)·ln(D_s/D_bore)/k_m, k_m = a + (b/2)(T1+T2) + (c/3)(T1²+T1·T2+T2²) — the exact mean of k(T) = a + bT + cT² between the interface and surface temperatures; D_s and D_bore from a built-in ASTM C585-style table (e.g. NPS 2: bore 2.41 in, 1 in → 4.50 in OD)

k_curves_used.note: a, b, c in k(T) = a + bT + cT², Btu·in/h·ft²·°F with T in °F; the page says "Thermal conductivity based on ASTM Specification Values"

equations.surface: h_s = h_rad + h_conv. h_rad = 0.1714·ε·[(T_s/100)⁴ − (T_a/100)⁴]/(T_s − T_a) (°R); ε = 0.8 for the bare pipe, Line 8 when insulated. h_conv: Churchill–Chu natural convection and Churchill–Bernstein forced convection (Re from wind mph × 5280 ft/h), combined Nu = [(Nu_F − 0.3)⁴ + (Nu_N − 0.3)⁴]^¼ + 0.3; air properties at the film temperature — the ASTM C680 forms.
equations.fuel_cost: Cost of Fuel ($/yr) = 100·|Heat Loss|·hours·fuel_cost/(fuel_btu·efficiency_pct); fuel_btu: gas 1,027,000 Btu/Mcf, oil 138,690 Btu/gal, propane 91,033 Btu/gal, coal 19,977,000 Btu/ton, electricity 3,412 Btu/kWh
equations.co2: CO2 (MT/yr) = |Heat Loss|·hours·fuel_co2/(efficiency_pct·22,000,000); not compared (the app has no emissions output)
equations.annual_energy: not printed by NIA; annual_heat_loss_btu_yr here = Heat Loss × hours, the product inside its cost formula

harness: main.js loaded unmodified into a Node vm context and driven as controller.js does (new ECalc(); fields set as gather_values() sets them, select values as strings; result_table()). The UI computes rows in order bare, 0.5 … 4 in., carrying the surface-temperature guess forward; the harness does the same. Check: the NIA default inputs (case NIA-1) reproduce every row of the published default-input screenshot (research/validation-cases.json CASE-13: bare 349°F/1443, 1 in 93/95, 1.5 in 87/70, 2 in 84/58, 2.5 in 82/50, 3 in 81/45, 3.5 in 80/40, 4 in 80/37 Btu/h) after the page's rounding to whole numbers. Values under result_table_verbatim are the unrounded numbers the page rounds for display (heat loss and surface temperature to whole numbers, costs as currency).
app_method: SimState = initialState('hot') with the case's pipe, temperatures, wind, insulation (kProduct = productForTemp, as the UI picks it), thickness, jacket/facing giving the same emittance (aluminum oxidized 0.10 or ASJ 0.90), run length and hours, and pipeOutdoors false (NIA prices one average ambient and wind over the hours entered); evaluate() → solveCase per side; annualCost() = |q|·length·hours ÷ efficiency × price. NIA gas $/Mcf is entered as $/MMBtu at NIA's own 1.027 MMBtu/Mcf.
findings: Cost/energy step: given NIA's own per-foot heat loss, the app's costSteps gives NIA's fuel cost exactly for gas (difference ≤ 2e-14 %) and 0.0041 % lower for electricity (3,412.14 vs NIA's 3,412 Btu/kWh).

Surface heat transfer is the same: with NIA's k-curve, insulation bore/OD and steel-wall resistance fed into solveCase, heat loss agrees to ≤ 0.002 % and surface temperature to ≤ 0.001°F on every case, bare and insulated.

Bare pipe as configured: the app is 0.11–0.78 % higher because it neglects the steel wall (as C680 does) while NIA includes it; the largest case (NPS 8 at 600°F) has a 2.2°F drop across the wall in NIA.

Insulated as configured: the app is 4.1–10.5 % lower. Most is k data — the app uses manufacturer typical k (OC SSL II; ROCKWOOL ProRox PS 960NA), 3.4–10.0 % below NIA's ASTM C547 specification curves at the layer mean temperature; the remaining 0.7–2.1 % is NIA's insulation bore (e.g. 2.41 in on NPS 2) versus the app's insulation-on-pipe-OD. Swapping in NIA's k leaves −0.7 to −2.1 %; adding NIA's bore/OD leaves +0.01 to +0.03 %.
Annual savings as configured: the app is 0.53–1.22 % higher than NIA (bare slightly higher, insulated lower; savings are dominated by the bare loss).
No discrepancy beyond these input-data differences was found.

tolerances_used_in_test.insulated_as_configured: −12 % to −3 % (observed −4.1 to −10.5 %; k data and bore), and within −2.5 % to 0 once NIA's k-curve is swapped in
